recognize_zh: 一團大型細胞彼此黏聚、共用淡紫灰色細顆粒狀細胞質而呈融合狀（syncytial），核大、卵圓形、染色質粗顆粒狀，細胞界線不清，形態與周圍零散的造血細胞不同，提示骨髓中的外來非造血腫瘤細胞。
features: Cohesive cluster of large cells with indistinct borders forming a syncytial-appearing aggregate
Large oval to round nuclei with coarsely granular, clumped chromatin; nucleoli not conspicuous at this resolution
Abundant pale lavender-grey, finely granular to microvacuolated shared cytoplasm
Mild nuclear size variation with some nuclear overlapping
Adjacent individual hematopoietic cells and red cells with drying artifact
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a cohesive, syncytial-appearing cluster of large cells with abundant pale, finely granular cytoplasm and indistinct cell borders. The nuclei are large and oval with coarsely granular chromatin and mild size variation. These cells differ in cohesion and cytology from the scattered hematopoietic elements. Findings are suggestive of metastatic non-hematopoietic tumor cells; immunohistochemistry on the core biopsy or clot section (e.g. cytokeratin, CD45) is needed for confirmation and lineage assignment.

ddx.vs: Osteoblasts are discrete cells with eccentric nuclei, a perinuclear hof set away from the nucleus, and deeper blue cytoplasm, rather than a syncytial clump with shared pale cytoplasm.
A megakaryocyte has a single multilobated nucleus, whereas this aggregate contains multiple separate nuclei from different cells.
Osteoclasts have many small uniform round nuclei with nucleoli, and macrophages contain phagocytosed debris, neither of which matches these large coarse-chromatin nuclei.

ddx.dx: Clumped plasma cells or lymphoma cells
ddx.vs: Hematopoietic neoplasms are usually discohesive with eccentric nuclei or basophilic cytoplasm and are CD45 or CD138 positive, unlike cohesive cytokeratin-positive epithelial clusters.
